parts.text:
We have the live HTML. Key issues: Accessibility (70): 1. `` has no `lang` attribute — Lighthouse flags "html-has-lang" (likely a major failure). 2. Images with `alt=""` on album art — these are meaningful images inside buttons; decorative alt is technically okay if button has accessible name. But buttons consist ONLY of an SVG icon (aria-hidden) → no accessible name. "button-name" failure — 6+ buttons (playback controls skip-back/play/forward), volume icon isn't a button though. Buttons 83,85,87 with only aria-hidden svg → unnamed. Also the "Click me" button is fine due to text. 3. Sliders: `` — no accessible label (empty span) → "label" failure for the volume/progress sliders. Note `data-event-listeners` doesn't help. Also multiple sliders unlabeled. 4. Color contrast: gray text `rgba(107,114,128,1)` (#6B7280) on light background (#F6F7FA / white) at 13px — contrast is 4.83:1 which passes AA for normal text... Actually #6B7280 on white is 4.83:1, passes. On #F6F7FA slightly lower ~4.65 passes. Hmm. But some are on album art backgrounds? Also `rgba(26,58,140)` on `rgba(232,239,255)` fine. Contrast may be flagged for text over image backgrounds—the album art images with text? No. However: text with opacity 0.666 (rgba(255,255,255,0.666)) on transparent over album art → contrast fail possibly. And the ghost player spans over image. 5. Heading order: page has only `

` (Library, Now Playing) and no `

` → "heading-order" / "page-has-heading-one" (best practice) and document has no h1. Actually SEO uses h1 too. 6. `

parts.text:
Let's read spec/OPCODE.md META section lines ~400-430 and the environment field family. Also check how color scheme/theme reset is supported end-to-end, as the template for a new META command. Then examine the renderer decode META handling (currently token scheme). The Java emitter and session. Also HTML head injection.

Also need to decide the metadata design. Something like:

`META::SET_DOCUMENT_METADATA` with fields? 16-byte opcode has A/B/C (3x u32) — strings live in arena. Could do one opcode per metadata field:
- `META::SET_DOCUMENT_TITLE` A=arenaRef(title string) 
- `META::SET_DOCUMENT_DESCRIPTION` A=arenaRef
- `META::SET_DOCUMENT_LANG` A=arenaRef (e.g. "en")
- `META::SET_DOCUMENT_CANONICAL` A=arenaRef (URL)
- maybe `META::SET_DOCUMENT_METADATA` with A=field id (u16), B=value type, C=arenaRef → extensible family like ENVIRONMENT. That's cleaner and future-proof (og:image, theme-color, robots). Using an extensible field family mirrors ENVIRONMENT. But then strings need arena refs in C. For value types: STRING arena ref, or maybe BOOL etc.

Alternatively one opcode `META::DOCUMENT` with A = field ID, B = [value type in low byte], C = arena offset. That mirrors `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` (A=arenaRef path, B=valueType, C=value). For document title it's simple: A=fieldId, B=valueType, C=arenaRef. Hmm SET_DESIGN_TOKEN uses A=path ref, B=type, C=value. For document field family: A=fieldId (u16), B=type, C=payload/arenaRef.

Need also to consider "runtime adjustable" with reactivity: the engine should re-emit a metadata opcode when a bound signal changes, and on route changes. parts.text:
Now decide the design surface for runtime-adjustable metadata.

Key design considerations:
- Protocol-first: add `META::DOCUMENT_METADATA` extensible field family (or separate commands). Guest → host (app → renderer).
- Data: title (string), description (string), lang (string), canonical (string), maybe robots (string), theme-color, og:*? Keep field family for extension.
- Reactivity: engine must bind metadata to signals, like text bindings; the app sets a signal → only metadata opcode emitted. Document metadata is global (not node-bound). Add a `document` binding slot in Engine: `set_document_field(field, signal)` records a signal → field dependency; on signal change, emit META opcode. Similar to how theme is static but set_signal is reactive.

How should the DSL author API look? Options:

Option A: `DocumentMetadata` value object with signals:
```java
View root = MusicPlayerView.make(...).modifiers(documentTitle(computed(...)), documentDescription(...), documentLang("en"))
```
or `.modifiers(document(d -> d.title(...).description(...)))` a modifier like theme/color scheme. But modifiers are applied to a View; a document modifier can be captured at mount and wired by the emitter. This mirrors `.modifiers(environmentBinding(...))` and theme.

Option B: a `Document` state object like MediaController:
```java
Document doc = new Document();
doc.title(computed(...));
...
root.modifiers(documentBinding(doc))
```
Not great.

Option C: a `Page`/`Scene` wrapper hosting metadata + root. More invasive.

Given the DSL has "modifiers" that can be pure values, Option A fits: a `DocumentMetadata` modifier value with config (title/description/lang/canonical each Signal<String>), built via `Modifiers.documentMetadata(d -> d.title(...))`, or single-value sugar `documentTitle(signal)`. But the doc says: "modifiers are ViewModifier values built by Modifiers facade lowercase functions" and environmentBinding is an example. This is consistent.

However, the user says "a route may need to specify a new title". In the DSL, routes are app-defined (route table). The app can make the title a computed signal over the router's path:
```java
var title = computed(() -> switch (router.path().get()) { case "/ad" -> "Ad"; default -> "Pathland"; });
Text... root.modifiers(documentMetadata(d -> d.title(title)))
```
This re-emits the title on route change. SSR: mount with the current active path, computed evaluates for that path → initial title. Good. Alternatively the route declarations themselves can carry title/description; but that would modify router API. The computed-signal approach avoids router changes and is general.

But maybe they want per-route declarative metadata: `Route.of("/x", view).title("X")`? Let's inspect the router API in Java/Rust. If routes are declared as data, adding metadata there is natural, but then runtime updates on navigation need router → metadata sync. Let's look.

The router has a signal; a computed title from `router.routeSignal()` works naturally. But per-route titles might be more ergonomic via RouteTable builder `.route(pattern, view)` plus metadata. However adding metadata to routes couples routing to document concerns and may not generalize to non-route changes (e.g. selected track might want title "Playing X"). Given the user says "Fx. a route may need to specify a new title" — an example, not the only case. A reactive document metadata binding is the general solution; routes can feed it.

Design proposal details:

Protocol:
- Add `META` command `SET_DOCUMENT_METADATA` (0x08 draft). Layout: `A = field id (u16 low)`, `B = value type (low byte)`, `C = value/arena ref`.
  - Fields: `DOCUMENT_TITLE = 0x0001` (STRING), `DOCUMENT_DESCRIPTION = 0x0002` (STRING), `DOCUMENT_LANG = 0x0003` (STRING), `DOCUMENT_CANONICAL = 0x0004` (STRING). Maybe `DOCUMENT_ROBOTS = 0x0005` (STRING) later; `DOCUMENT_THEME_COLOR` enum? Keep only four now + extensible.
  - Alternative: separate commands per field (`SET_DOCUMENT_TITLE`, `SET_DOCUMENT_DESCRIPTION`, ...) with A/B/C = string offset. Simpler decoding, but "new field = new command" — the spec prefers extensible families (environment). Use field family.
  - String encoding: arena ref with dual convention (absolute over ring, relative in network batch) like NAVIGATE/TEXT_CHANGED/SET_TEXT. But note: design tokens use arenaRef and the renderer gets `strings` section; for the ring, the host decodes in place? Actually the HTML renderer's `decode` gets `strings: &[u8]` (whole arena?) and `strings_str` uses offsets. Need to confirm whether absolute/relative distinction matters for renderer (network batches have a string section and offset is relative). Look at how `SET_TEXT` is decoded to understand. Important for plan accuracy.
  - Clearing a field: empty string or a "null" flag? Use empty string = clear (title falls back to default/empty). Or flags bit to remove. Simpler: empty string clears.
- Semantics: renderer updates the document metadata for subsequent document render; SSR head includes them; DOM client applies them to `document.title`, `<meta name=description>`, `<html lang>`, `<link rel=canonical>`. This is host state (document), not retained tree state; allowed under stateless renderers? It's output metadata, similar to color scheme/theme — renderer-global, not app state. It's a cache of renderer output, fine.
- SSR: metadata opcodes in the mount frame; HTML renderer reads them when building `<head>`.
- Runtime: DOM client handles opcodes in deltas; updates DOM head; no tree re-render.
- Native renderers (GTK/Qt): map to window title (GTK `set_title`, Qt `Window.title`), ignore description/lang/canonical (or apply to window title only). GTK/Qt don't have SEO; use title for window/taskbar.
- Proxy views: metadata from a proxied app? Probably ignore/proxy's metadata shouldn't override host document; spec PROXY should state metadata opcodes from the origin are dropped during merge (or namespaced?). Need to address: `FrameMerger` might merge META opcodes. Document metadata is host-document-global; a proxied origin's title must not overwrite the host page title. So define: metadata from proxy snapshots is ignored (except the top-level app). But maybe a proxied app is a whole page embedded? Here it's a widget. Plan should specify dropping META::SET_DOCUMENT_METADATA from proxy frames during merge. Check FrameMerger to see if it filters tokens (tokens from proxy are merged into head). parts.text:
Metadata modifier would implement ViewModifier.body(View) returning a wrapper that collects metadata into Environment? But it needs to be discovered by Emitter at mount regardless of depth. Similar to theme? Theme isn't a modifier; passed to session. `ButtonStyle`/navigation are applied structurally.

For document metadata, the natural place is not a per-subtree modifier but a root-level binding. Options:
1. `DocumentMetadata` as a `ViewModifier` whose wrapper view contributes to a thread-local/Environment collector during render, then Emitter reads it after `root.render(env)`. The emitter already renders the tree; a wrapper `MetadataView` could register itself in `Environment` (like environment state scope) and the Emitter reads `env.documentMetadata()` after render. But multiple wrappers — nearest/last wins? Document is global; define last-declared wins. More complexity.
2. `Emitter`/`PathlandSession` API: `session.documentMetadata(meta)` after mount, plus `Emitter.setDocumentMetadata(...)` registers signal effects that emit META opcodes. The app can call it in its root factory? `PathlandApp.newRoot()` returns a View only; the route may change. But the app can compute title from router signal and pass a signal into a modifier.
3. `DocumentMetadata` on `PathlandApp` interface method returning a `DocumentMetadata` object with signals. The session mounts then binds. But route title changes still work because signals. `PathlandApp` is the app; adding `default DocumentMetadata metadata() { return null; }` fits (like `theme()`). The title signal can be derived from router state? The router is created inside the root view, so the app can't easily access it in `metadata()` unless it owns the router. Hmm.

So the modifier approach (applied to the root view) is more ergonomic for per-route computed titles. But the emitter and Rust engine both need a "document" concept.

Alternative: Treat metadata as a new **component** `DOCUMENT` (non-visual, like MEDIA_CONTROLLER) with node properties? E.g. a `DOCUMENT_METADATA` non-visual node owning title/description/lang/canonical as string properties, materialized once in the tree; renderer finds it and uses it for the head; a signal bound property updates emit `SET_PROPERTY` (already exists!) and the DOM client applies it to the document. This is elegant:
- No new META commands! Reuse `PARAMETER::SET_PROPERTY` with a non-visual `DOCUMENT` component (e.g. 0x31) and new property ids `DOCUMENT_TITLE`, `DOCUMENT_DESCRIPTION`, `DOCUMENT_LANG`, `DOCUMENT_CANONICAL` (STRING).
- Reactive updates: bind a string property to a signal (`Node::string_binding`) → emits `SET_PROPERTY` for the document node → renderer updates `<head>` / `document.title`.
- SSR: the HTML renderer scans for the document node while rendering and emits head with metadata.
- GTK/Qt: find the document node and set window title (title property), ignore rest.
- Proxy: origin's document node would be embedded in the host tree — need to ignore nested document nodes (only the root app's top-level document node counts). Could specify "renderer uses the first/nearest DOCUMENT node; proxied subtrees' DOCUMENT nodes are ignored" or just treat like a normal non-visual node and don't let proxy create one.
- Downsides: document metadata is renderer-global state, not tree state; modeling it as a node bends "renderer must not retain app state" slightly but it's still an emitted command. Also "document" isn't a view; but MEDIA_CONTROLLER precedent exists (state object → non-visual node). However the component ID space and specs are for UI primitives; a document metadata node is arguably a "utility" component.
- Reactivity: per-property string bindings already supported in engine/Java emitter, so runtime title updates are trivial. This is a big win.
- But the DOM client currently applies SET_PROPERTY to the node element; a document node would have a hidden DOM element? We'd need to special-case the document component: create no element (or a `<meta>`/`title` sink) and route property updates to document head. Could materialize head elements directly: `DOCUMENT` node could render into `<title>`, `<meta name=description>`, `<html lang>`, `<link rel=canonical>`; updates to the node id map to those elements. But one node has multiple properties mapping to different elements. The renderer's id→element map assumes one element. It could create a hidden `<div data-pathland-id>`? Then apply properties to it and a special "apply document meta" hook. TS applyStringProperty would need special handling. Doable but hacky.
- `SET_PROPERTY` on a non-visual node is already used for MEDIA_CONTROLLER (string props). The DOM apply has special handling for media. Similar path for document. Then no protocol META addition; just a component + properties. But does this respect "declarative, not positioned"? Yes, it describes document metadata as properties.

Alternative to non-visual node: new `META` family is cleaner semantically (document is not part of the view tree), and mirrors `SET_COLOR_SCHEME`/`RESET_THEME` which are renderer-wide, already handled by META. Runtime reactivity is the only extra machinery: engine needs dependency tracking for document fields (it's not hard: a `document_deps: [Option<SignalId>; N]` + set_document_field/emit; Java emitter creates an effect per metadata field and emits META opcodes).

Which to choose? Let's weigh:

META approach:
+ Semantically correct: document metadata is renderer-wide/host state, not a tree node.
+ Extensible field family matches ENVIRONMENT precedent.
+ Doesn't add a fake component to the tree or a hidden DOM node.
+ Long-term fits `<title>`, `<meta>`, OG tags, canonical, lang, robots.
+ SSR head generation straightforward: scan META ops into a `DocumentMeta` struct during decode; then build head.
+ Runtime updates: Java `Emitter` can hold a small `DocumentMetadataBinding` registry; Rust `Engine` can track signal deps.
- More code: new constants, encoder/decoder, engine dependency slot, Java emitter, TS apply, GTK/Qt, FrameRebase.
- SSR frame merger: must ignore proxy metadata (filter command).

Node/property approach:
+ Reuses existing reactive string-property plumbing (zero new emit machinery).
+ Uses existing SET_PROPERTY; renderer decode already stores strings on nodes.
- Adds a pseudo-component and property IDs to the protocol.
- DOM client must special-case node (hidden element or direct head sync).
- "A document node inside the tree" is conceptually odd; route swaps could remove the node and lose metadata; multiple nested apps conflict.
- Proxy collision risk.

I lean META. The user explicitly wants runtime updates per route; META with signal bindings is clean. It also matches how theme/scheme runtime works (`Emitter.setColorScheme` emits META). We can model `DocumentMetadata` as a modifier that needs no node: the emitter can discover it at mount. But how? Modifiers are applied by wrapping views with `Modified`/`*View` wrappers that alter rendering. A metadata modifier cannot produce a node; it needs a side channel.

Option: extend `Environment` with a mutable `DocumentMetadataSink` available during render; the modifier wrapper calls `env.setDocumentMetadata(...)` when rendered, and the Emitter reads it after `tree = root.render(env)`. Since `body()` is evaluated at mount, the modifier wrapper's `body()`/render can register signals. But route changes need the binding to re-evaluate; signals are bound, so the metadata sink records the signals and the emitter registers effects. The wrapper is fine. This mirrors `PersistentState.connect(this)` in View.render. So:
- `DocumentMetadata` ViewModifier wraps the content, and during render sets `env.document(meta)` (or pushes into a collector). The wrapper renders its content unchanged. Emitter after render reads `env.documentMetadata()` and binds.
- But if the modifier is on a subtree that is structurally swapped (e.g. inside a route), then it should apply only while that subtree is mounted, and revert when removed. That's actually desirable: per-route metadata naturally! But the Emitter's structural reconcile re-renders a subtree with the same `env`; after reconcile, read the active metadata and emit if changed. Need a mechanism to recompute active metadata after structural changes (or use Environment scoping + effect when metadata is set). Complexity: when a route's subtree with `.documentMetadata(...)` is removed, the old metadata should revert to the parent/root's. A global sink approach can recompute on every render pass.

Simpler and more predictable: metadata is declared on the **root** view only (like theme), and route-dependent values come from computed signals. Document metadata is page-global. Enforce "root-level". Then no structural scoping issues. The API can be `.modifiers(documentMetadata(...))` applied anywhere but the emitter only honors the outermost/root one (or the last applied). Document this as a root modifier.

Even simpler: add to `PathlandApp`:
```java
default DocumentMetadata document() { return DocumentMetadata.empty(); }
```
But route applications own the router inside the root view; however the route's title can be computed if the app creates the router outside and passes it in. The existing demos create the router inside the root view? Let's check Navigation/SplitNavDemo. But `PathlandApp.newRoot()` can return `new RootView(router)` with router owned by the app instance. Yet each session needs its own router (per-session state), and `newRoot()` is per session, so the app would construct the router inside newRoot, and then can't pass a metadata object that references it to `document()` (separate call). Unless `newRoot()` returns a `View` that carries metadata.

So root view modifier is best. Design:

Let me consider another important aspect: SSR + client-side route changes. In this app, navigation is client-side; the DOM client receives deltas. Document metadata updates must arrive as opcodes. That confirms protocol-level metadata.

Where do we store the "current document metadata" for SSR? HTML renderer receives a frame; decode sees META ops. But the SSR frame merges proxies. Also `META::RESET` clears; metadata should persist through RESET? Document metadata is renderer state; RESET only clears rendered output (nodes), not document metadata/theme. Define: metadata survives RESET; a snapshot re-emits it (renderFull) so a reconnect is fine. If nothing emitted, SSR fallback title remains "Pathland".

Runtime dedupe: track last emitted per field in engine/emitter (like snapshot) so set_signal with unchanged value emits 0. Java emitter can compare lastMeta values.

Clearing a field: title can't be empty ideally; empty → renderer default. Specify empty string clears.

Security/escaping: title/description/canonical/lang must be HTML-escaped (already escape functions). Canonical URL validation? Renderer should escape. Lang validation maybe.

Canonical per route: needs absolute URL (SSR host knows origin). The app can compute from route; but the app doesn't know the origin (renderer/host does). Options: allow relative canonical and let host resolve, or add the origin to the environment. For the plan: canonical is a string; SSR host can resolve relative to the request origin (PathlandSession / IndexResource has URI info? currently render only route). Alternatively skip canonical for now (not requested). Title/description/lang are requested. I'd include canonical as optional future field but maybe implement now to fix SEO. Canonical needs the request absolute URL; the starter can supply origin via a new `Platform` env field or the app can build it from `Platform.ACTIVE_PATH` + configured base URL. Hmm. Since host knows request URL, add an env field `URL`/`ORIGIN`? That's scope creep. Instead, canonical could be emitted by the app with an absolute base configured in the app. Or defer canonical. Lighthouse canonical is manual (not scored) in v12. So defer canonical; focus on title/description/lang. Maybe add field anyway for future.

Also description needs to be set per route. Title default and template? App decides.

Another consideration: `lang` per route — include.

Also OG/Twitter tags? Not requested. Extensible family allows later.

Now, what about the JS DOM client updating `<title>` at runtime? It should also update after hydration: the SSR HTML already contains the title; on navigation deltas apply. Need `applyMeta` handle the new command and string offsets (batch.strings). Title field is in `op.c` (relative/absolute strings). The `applyBatch` passes `batch.strings` to applyStyle; `applyMeta(op, r)` currently doesn't get strings. Change signature to `applyMeta(op, batch.strings, r)`. Also `describe.ts` for debugging. Constants.

Also `DomRenderer` should not retain application state; keeping document title in the DOM is renderer output. Fine.

Also the TS client sends environment etc. No metadata from client.

Rust core: constants, doc, conformance vectors, zero-alloc? Emitting metadata on signal change allocates strings in the arena (same as SET_TEXT), acceptable? Steady-state emission for text currently allocates? They claim zero dynamic heap allocations during steady-state, but arena writes are fine. `set_signal` already arena-allocates strings.

Engine: Add:
```rust
#[derive(Default)]
struct DocumentBinding { title: Option<SignalId>, description: ..., lang: ... }
```
In `set_signal`, when a changed signal feeds a document field, emit metadata. How does a signal know? Add `engine.bind_document_field(field, SignalId)` — records dep. Simpler: `Engine::set_document(field, SignalId)` similar to `node.bind_text`. On set_signal, after node deps, check document deps. Or reuse the runtime's dependency graph: document deps are not nodes. Add a `Dep::Document { field }` variant? The runtime's `node_deps` is node-specific. Probably simpler to keep a separate map `document: [Option<SignalId>; 4]` and in `set_signal`, if any field maps to the changed signal (or a computed that depends on it — `changed` includes transitively invalidated computed ids), emit field op. Need to check `Runtime::set` returns changed ids including computeds. Then compare to last emitted string; emit.

The Rust DSL surface: add a `document` modifier? The Rust view tree is a `Node`; modifiers mutate nodes. A document modifier can't attach to a node cleanly — unless it sets a marker on the root node. Alternative Rust engine API: `engine.document_metadata(title_signal, desc_signal, lang_signal)` called before emit. Optionally a `ViewExt::document_metadata()` wrapper that records... but Rust's tree build doesn't have environment collection. Given the user's focus on route title in the Java/server demo, plan can include:
- Core/protocol + HTML + TS + Java DSL/emitter + starters (full web path).
- Rust engine bindings + GTK/Qt window title as part of the same change if we want parity.
We should ask about scope. But the plan should be comprehensive. I'll propose parity across Rust and Java, but note GTK/Qt only use title.

Wait: The GTK native window title; `pathland-render-gtk` likely sets window title in `run` from app name. Runtime title mapping would be a nice feature.

Now, API design preference. Let me propose two authoring options for the user:

Option 1 (recommended): **Document metadata as a root `ViewModifier` with reactive fields**
```java
VStack.children(...)
  .modifiers(documentMetadata(d -> d
      .title(computed(() -> titleFor(router.path())))
      .description(computed(() -> descriptionFor(router.path())))
      .language("en")))
```
- Emits `META::SET_DOCUMENT_METADATA` at mount and on signal changes.
- Route changes that swap subtrees can put `.documentMetadata(...)` on the route's view; the emitter re-reads active metadata after structural reconciliation and emits the change. If we support per-subtree scoping, the nearest active metadata wins, and removal reverts to the parent's — this gives "a route specifies a new title" declaratively.

Option 2: **Route table metadata**
```java
Navigation.table()
  .route("/", new HomeView()).title("Home").description("...")
```
- Router automatically emits metadata on navigation; no signals needed.
- But metadata tied to routes only; modals/dialogs/selection changes can't adjust title. More coupling.

Option 3: **Programmatic session/engine API**
```java
session.setDocumentTitle(signal) // or emitter
```
- Least DSL-friendly; app must wire manually; no SSR unless mount emits.

I recommend Option 1 with root-level (or route-scoped) modifier. Need to decide the scoping and how the emitter discovers the active metadata after structural changes. Let's think about feasibility in the Java emitter:

The Emitter's structural reconciliation re-renders a subtree via `root.render(env)` or a `structuralContent` render. If `DocumentMetadata` is a ViewModifier wrapper, the wrapper's `body()` wraps content. When rendered, it can call `env.registerDocumentMetadata(this)`. But `env` is shared; multiple nested wrappers would each register. Need "last registration during a render pass wins" — but when does a pass boundary occur? `Emitter.mount` calls `root.render(env)` once. Structural reconcile re-renders only a subtree, but metadata nested inside that subtree should become active; metadata outside should remain. A simple register-on-render is order-dependent and stale (removed metadata remains). Could have `Environment` maintain a stack scoped during render: `env.withDocumentMetadata(meta, () -> content.render(env))` which pushes/pops; then after the full render, `env.documentMetadata()` is the outermost/root or last-declared. But nested route content renders after the root wrapper, so during the render, the inner wrapper is active, then pops, leaving the outer metadata — so outermost wins, meaning a route's inner `.documentMetadata` would be ignored. If we want route-scoped override, we'd need to capture the deepest one. Hmm.

Alternative: metadata modifier is applied to the **root view** and the root view's body computes per-route metadata. In the demo, `MusicPlayerView` is the root and can bind metadata signals computed from the router. That's simple and predictable. Per-route views do not declare metadata. This still satisfies "a route may need a new title" because the metadata signal is computed from the route. I'll recommend this.

How does the root modifier register with the emitter? The root view is `MusicPlayerView.make(...).modifiers(documentMetadata(...))`. `Modified` wraps it; the Emitter mounts the wrapped view, and `env` is passed. A `DocumentMetadataView` could implement `render(env)`:

env.setDocumentMetadata(config); // record
return node;
```
Since it wraps only the root, no scoping conflict. Document that it's a root-level modifier (ignored on non-root? or last wrapper wins). The emitter reads `env.documentMetadata()` after `root.render(env)`. For `renderFull`, it re-emits the last bound metadata. For runtime, bind each field's signal effect.

SSR: `Emitter.mount` emits metadata opcodes before the tree (after theme) so HTML head has it. Order doesn't matter for head generation, but emit at start.

Now what about the app-level route signal? `MusicPlayerView` has the router. The metadata modifier can be applied in its `body()`? For Rust DSL parity: the Rust `ViewModifier` trait mutates a `Node`; metadata can't be per-node. Add an `Engine` binding API:
```rust
let title = engine.computed(...);
engine.document(DocumentMetadata::new().title(title).description(desc).lang("en"));

and on `set(signal)` the engine emits. This is analogous to `engine.bind_text`. Maybe a `pathland_view::document(DocumentMetadata)` root wrapper that collects into a thread-local during tree build? <html lang="en" data-pathland-scheme=...>
<head>
...
<title>{title}</title>
<meta name="description" content="{desc}">

That's fine but brittle. Better: change the Rust renderer to accept `html_attrs` (or have the session insert before the first `>` of the html tag). E.g. `html.replaceFirst("<html", "<html data-pathland-base=...")`. Use `replaceFirst` with literal quote. Fine. Note in plan.

- Title escaping: escape HTML text; description/canonical attribute escaping.

- Update `data-pathland-ssr-scoped` etc. unchanged.

- When no metadata opcodes: fallback title "Pathland" and no description/lang? For lang, default "en"? Most apps are English; docs note. Or use `lang=""` invalid. I'd default `lang="en"` (HTML spec recommends a valid lang). Also the app can override at runtime.

- The DOM client `applyMeta` must update `document.documentElement.lang`, `<title>`, `<meta name=description>` (create if missing), `<link rel=canonical>` (create if missing/remove if empty). Also initialization: SSR has them. On RESET, keep metadata. On full snapshot after reconnect, re-emitted metadata updates.

Add filter in FrameMerger. Also in the live proxy path, proxy deltas are forwarded? The proxy forwarding remaps opcodes (line 293-345). Need to filter metadata commands there too. Good plan detail.

Now think about "runtime adjustable title/description" for the **SSR** request: the session mounts per request with the route, so the computed title sees the route → SSR head correct. The Java emitter emits metadata opcodes at mount; HTML renderer decodes → head. Good.

What about app-level `PathlandApp`/metadata? Not needed.

What about documents with no navigation (GTK demo)? Engine API emits metadata; GTK renderer sets window title; no description usage.

Now, an important question: META commands are guest→host. The HTML renderer is a pure function of a frame. Decoding metadata into a struct is fine.

Do we want a single command with an extensible field family, or one command per field? Let's settle: `META::SET_DOCUMENT_METADATA` (0x08) with `A = field id (u16)`, `B = value type (low byte)`, `C = value` (STRING → arena/string-section offset; the field family can later carry BOOL/enums). Mirrors `SET_PROPERTY` (property id + value type + value) and `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`. Actually `SET_PROPERTY` uses A=nodeId, B=(type<<16)|propId, C=value. We could mimic exactly: A = 0 (no node), B = (valueType<<16)|fieldId, C = value. That's more consistent with the existing parameter family and avoids a separate 16-bit field limit? For META, A can be the field id. Let's define: `A = field id (u16, low)`, `B = value type (low byte)`, `C = value`. Wait `META::ENVIRONMENT` uses A=fieldId, B=field value, C=0 (no type; environment fields are typed by field). For document metadata all fields are strings initially, but future ones (e.g. theme-color) could be colors. Use `A=fieldId`, `B=valueType`, `C=payload`. Clean.

Fields:
- `DOCUMENT_TITLE = 0x0001` STRING
- `DOCUMENT_DESCRIPTION = 0x0002` STRING
- `DOCUMENT_LANGUAGE = 0x0003` STRING (BCP 47)
- `DOCUMENT_CANONICAL = 0x0004` STRING (absolute URL)
- `DOCUMENT_ROBOTS = 0x0005` STRING ("noindex" etc.) — future
Empty string clears.

Should title/description/lang be one opcode each? Yes, one opcode per field (extensible family). A route change may emit 1-3 opcodes.

Ordering/atomicity: all in one frame → apply together. Fine.

SSR fallback: title default "Pathland" currently. When metadata absent, keep `<title>Pathland</title>`; add `lang="en"` default. Description absent → omit meta tag. Hmm, but SEO requires description; apps should set it. The renderer can't invent one.

What about `META::RESET`: keep metadata (document-level, like theme/scheme). `renderFull` re-emits metadata before the tree so a resync restores it (the DOM client keeps it anyway, but a fresh hydration from a full snapshot needs it). Define metadata is renderer state and is NOT cleared by RESET (consistent with color scheme/theme). Actually `META::RESET` says "clear all rendered output" — metadata is not rendered output? It's document state. The DOM client's CMD_RESET clears byId but not title. Fine.

Now the DSL API specifics. Follow the configurator convention:
```java
// com.pathland.view.DocumentMetadata implements ViewModifier
public final class DocumentMetadata implements ViewModifier {
  public static final class Config {
    public Config title(String/Signal<String>);
    public Config description(String/Signal<String>);
    public Config language(String/Signal<String>);
    public Config canonical(String/Signal<String>);
  }
  public static DocumentMetadata of(...)? No: "make" convention? Modifiers built via Modifiers facade lowercase functions.
}
```
`Modifiers.documentMetadata(Consumer<Config>)` returns `DocumentMetadata.with(...)`. Single-value shortcuts? Multi-member config → lambda only. Also maybe convenience `Modifiers.documentTitle(...)`? To keep the vocabulary minimal, one `documentMetadata(...)`.

But the doc convention says custom value types with a config expose `static ViewBuilder make` for views and lowercase static factory on the style type; for modifiers the `Modifiers` facade. So `Modifiers.documentMetadata(d -> ...)`.

Implementation of the wrapper: `DocumentMetadata implements ViewModifier` with `body(View content)` returning a `DocumentMetadataView` that renders content and records itself into `Environment` (needs access to `Environment`). `View.render(Environment)` can do this. Alternatively, simpler: `DocumentMetadata` is a `ViewModifier` that wraps content in a composite `View` whose `render(env)` calls `env.documentMetadata(this)` then `content.render(env)`. Add `Environment.setDocumentMetadata(DocumentMetadata)`; emitter reads after render.

But `Environment` is also used by views and is passed to `render`. Good.

Enforcement of root-only: The emitter reads whatever the last `setDocumentMetadata` call was during the root render; since modifiers apply outermost-first? `Modified.apply` wraps: `modifiers(A,B)` → A outermost? Let's check `Modified.apply`: `result = Modified.apply(result, modifier)` loops, so each new modifier wraps the previous → B outermost. During render, the outermost wrapper calls `env.set` then renders inner, and an inner metadata wrapper may overwrite. So if only root, no issue. If nested, deepest (last rendered) wins. Document as "applies document-wide; the innermost declaration wins" — acceptable. But removal of a subtree leaves stale env metadata unless we reset at the start of each render pass. Emitter should clear `env.documentMetadata` before `root.render(env)` each mount; structural re-renders don't re-render the root, so a route-scoped inner metadata wouldn't be removed. To avoid complexity, document root-only and do not support route-subtree scoping; compute from signals instead. In the Emitter, reset metadata before root render; nested declarations are undefined/innermost. Fine.

Alternatively, don't use a modifier at all; add `DocumentMetadata` as a first-class argument to `Emitter.mount(root, env, metadata)` via `PathlandApp.document()`... but route computed signals are inaccessible. Hmm, actually the app could create the metadata signals in `newRoot()` and... no, `newRoot()` only returns View.

I think root modifier is the pragmatic choice.

Rust side:
- `pathland-engine::Engine` add `document: DocumentMetadata` with signal ids and last values; `Engine::bind_document(DocumentMetadata)` (a struct of `Signal<String>` fields). Actually reuse `Node::string_binding` style. Rust DSL ergonomics:

parts.text:
No window metadata. We need platform-neutral naming. Let's think about what the concept is:

- The host window/surface that contains the UI has presentation metadata: title, subtitle, description (for accessibility/SEO), locale/language, maybe icon, represented file, modified state. The most general protocol category might be `META::SET_WINDOW_*`. Many UI toolkits have:
  - GTK: `GtkWindow:title`, `GtkHeaderBar:title/subtitle`
  - Qt: `QWindow:title`
  - macOS: `NSWindow:title`, `subtitle`, `representedFilename`, `documentEdited`
  - Windows: `SetWindowText`
  - Android: `Activity:title` / `setTitle`
  - Web: `document.title`
  - TUI/terminal: window title escape sequence
So "window" is platform-neutral enough and matches the user's suggestion: "other renderers has some support for setting title/description of the current window/app".

Maybe name the command `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` with field family:
- `WINDOW_TITLE` (STRING)
- `WINDOW_SUBTITLE` (STRING) — GTK headerbar, macOS subtitle
- `WINDOW_DESCRIPTION` (STRING) — browser `meta description`; native accessibility description/tooltip; may be ignored
- `WINDOW_LOCALE` (STRING) — browser `lang`; native locale/accessibility
- Later: `WINDOW_ICON` (STRING/arena image ref?), `WINDOW_MODIFIED` (U32 bool), `WINDOW_REPRESENTED_FILE` (STRING).

Wait, the user says "title/description of the current window/app". Maybe they mean two fields: title + description. Good.

Naming of the DSL modifier: `.modifiers(windowMetadata(w -> w.title(...).description(...).locale(...)))` or `.modifiers(appMetadata(...))`, `.modifiers(sceneMetadata(...))`. Since the protocol calls it window metadata, use `windowMetadata`. But in a web app, "window" maps to the document. Fine.

Alternatively `META::SET_PRESENTATION` / `SET_SHELL`? Overkill.

Consider naming fields `TITLE`, `SUBTITLE`, `DESCRIPTION`, `LOCALE`. The description field: For browsers, meta description; for native, could be the window subtitle? Better to have both `SUBTITLE` and `DESCRIPTION` to avoid conflating:
- `SUBTITLE`: a short secondary line displayed in the window chrome (macOS/GTK).
- `DESCRIPTION`: longer human-readable description (browser meta description, accessibility help).
Native renderer can ignore DESCRIPTION if no place. This is clean.

Language/locale: `LOCALE` (BCP 47). Browser maps to `lang`; native maps to app locale/accessibility. This is platform-neutral. The user only asked title/description; locale is still needed for the `html-has-lang` a11y failure. But is locale window metadata? It's more "content locale". Could be a separate META field family `SET_LOCALE` or an environment field (host→guest) instead. Hmm: Language of the content is authored by the app, so guest→host. But is it "window metadata"? Reasonable to include in the same family as `LOCALE`. Or add a separate `META::SET_LOCALE`. I'd include it in the family for simplicity, documented as content locale.

Canonical: omit (web-specific). The web host can derive canonical from the request route or a web-specific host extension. Note in plan: canonical stays host/web-owned (not protocol), e.g. the starter computes it from the request URL + configured origin, not from app opcodes. If per-route canonical is needed, the route-to-title mapping also gives the route, so the host can derive. Good; this avoids polluting the protocol.

Robots meta: web-specific; host controls via HTTP headers or config, not protocol. Fine.

So revised protocol:
```
META (0x04)
SET_WINDOW_METADATA = 0x08 (draft)
A = fieldId (u16 low)
B = valueType (low byte)  [STRING for now]
C = value (string offset; same convention as SET_TEXT: arena/batch section)
Fields:
  WINDOW_TITLE       0x0001 STRING
  WINDOW_SUBTITLE    0x0002 STRING
  WINDOW_DESCRIPTION 0x0003 STRING
  WINDOW_LOCALE      0x0004 STRING
```
Empty string clears/restores renderer default. Renderer mapping:
- Browser: title→`document.title` (and `<title>`); subtitle→nothing? maybe `og:title`? No. Description→`<meta name=description content>`; locale→`<html lang>`.
   Hmm, subtitle in browser has no standard place; could be ignored or used for `og:site_name`? Don't. Ignore.
   Wait, but browser: `<meta property="og:title">` could use title. Not needed.
- GTK4: title→window/headerbar title; subtitle→headerbar subtitle; description→accessibility description/tooltip? maybe ignore; locale→ignore/accessibility.
- Qt: title→window title; subtitle→window title suffix? maybe `title — subtitle`; description→ignore; locale→ignore.
- HTML server renderer: title/description/locale emitted in head; subtitle ignored.
- TUI: title→terminal title; etc.

Now the DSL:
- `WindowMetadata` implements ViewModifier, root-scoped, reactive Signal<String> fields: `title`, `subtitle`, `description`, `locale`. `Modifiers.windowMetadata(w -> ...)`.
- Alternatively name `ShellMetadata`/`SceneMetadata`. The user said "window/app". I'll go with `windowMetadata` and fields.

Hmm, is "window" appropriate for server-side HTML (no window)? The HTML renderer maps to document title. The concept "window/app metadata" covers it. The spec can define "the host window or app shell hosting this UI" — on the web, the browser tab/document.

Protocol spec section name: "Window metadata" under META. Fields table.

Now the reactivity/emitter plan stays the same, just renamed. The Java DSL types: `WindowMetadata`, `Modifiers.windowMetadata(...)`, `Environment.setWindowMetadata`. Emitter binds signals → `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`.

Now, one more thought: Should we instead express title/description as **semantic properties on the root node** (`ROLE` etc.)? No, window metadata isn't node-level.

Also, should title be per **route** or per **window**? Window. Route changes update the window metadata via signals. Good.

Now consider multi-window/multi-session: each host surface is its own opcode stream; metadata belongs to that stream. Fine.

Now the user's broader point: "The protocol cannot be browser specific." So also avoid `SET_HTML_LANG`, `SET_META_DESCRIPTION`. Use window/app concepts and document the mappings as renderer-specific. Good.

Should we call the field `DESCRIPTION` or `SUBTITLE`? The user explicitly says title/description. So `WINDOW_DESCRIPTION`. Native renderers: GTK could map description to `GtkWindow` accessibility? GTK4 has `accessible-role`/`accessible-label`; a window has a title; a description could go to the headerbar subtitle or be ignored. Document mapping as "renderer-defined; may be used for the window subtitle, accessibility description, or tooltip."

Wait—if we have both SUBTITLE and DESCRIPTION, native renderers may not know what to do. Maybe only TITLE + DESCRIPTION + LOCALE. Description on GTK → headerbar subtitle; browser → meta description. That's a sensible mapping: "a short human-readable description of the current content" maps to subtitle in native chrome and meta description on web. That avoids a redundant field. But macOS has both subtitle and (no description). Hmm.

Lighthouse SEO needs `meta description`; title/description alone suffice. Simplicity: fields `TITLE`, `DESCRIPTION`, `LOCALE`. Description maps to:
- web: `<meta name="description">`
- GTK/Qt: window subtitle (if supported) or ignored
- accessibility: content description.
That's a general "what this window shows" descriptor. I'd propose TITLE + DESCRIPTION + LOCALE, with SUBTITLE deferred/future. The user said title/description. Keep it minimal.

But is "description" of a window a real concept? The user themselves says "other renderers has some support for setting title/description of the current window/app" — so they're comfortable. Great.

Now the plan should explicitly say: the protocol names the concept; the browser renderer is a mapping, not the definition. Include mapping table.

Let me also think about the **app-level** naming: `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` vs `META::SET_APP_METADATA`. A window is a surface; an app may have multiple windows. The opcode stream is per-surface (per ring/session). So "window" is precise. For SSR, the document is the window. Good. Maybe `SET_SURFACE_METADATA`. I'll offer `SET_WINDOW_METADATA` as recommended.

Now revise the plan text. Also note the previous plan's `documentMetadata` DSL name would change to `windowMetadata`.

Let me ensure there isn't an existing notion in the DSL spec of `navigationTitle` (SwiftUI `.navigationTitle`). SwiftUI has `.navigationTitle(_:)` and `.navigationSubtitle` for the nav bar, not window title. But the GTK/Qt renderers use route as the nav page title. Hmm—there's a subtlety: on native, a navigation container's page title is route-derived. Window title is separate. In SwiftUI, `.navigationTitle` sets the title of the current screen. The protocol has `NAV_*` properties? Let's check for NAV_TITLE; earlier grep found none. GTK uses route directly. So window metadata maps to the top-level window, while nav page titles remain route-derived. For the browser, document.title should probably be the same as the current screen title; the app can set it.

Should we reuse a "screen title" concept instead of window? iOS navigation bar title, Android app bar title, browser document title. That's the "current view title". But the user says "current window/app". Keep window.

Another thought: The user's phrasing "Surely other renderers has some support for setting title/description of the current window/app" suggests they want the protocol concept named generically, and the browser maps to title/meta. Yes.

Now, the plan should incorporate accessibility/SEO fixes from the prior turn that are independent of metadata:
- lang → now via WINDOW_LOCALE (browser maps to `<html lang>`).
- title/description → WINDOW_TITLE/WINDOW_DESCRIPTION.
- `button-name`/`label`/`contrast`/`h1`/`region` remain.
- robots.txt/sitemap remain host-level (not protocol).

We can note that these still need fixing.

Now, the **runtime reactivity** details:
- Java emitter binds each field's signal; on change emit one META opcode; SSR mount emits initial values; renderFull re-emits.
- Rust engine binds fields; on `set_signal` emits; `emit` re-emits on change (or at mount).
- Native C ABI: the Java DSL's ring sink supports META pushes (add a `setWindowMetadata` to `OpcodeSink`/`FrameOpcodeSink`/`RingOpcodeSink`). Check `RingOpcodeSink` and `OpcodeSink` interfaces to include.
- C ABI for signal-based hosts? The native C ABI `pathland_native_*` exposes signals; the Rust engine handles it. The Java `ffm` ring uses `pathland_ring_buffer_push` for raw opcodes, so the Java emitter can push the metadata opcode and allocate strings via the core arena. Check `RingOpcodeSink.setString`/alloc. Fine.

Now, **SSR head generation**: The HTML renderer already decodes tokens from META. Add window metadata to the decode struct and head. It emits `<html lang>` only if locale set; else default "en"? For a11y, default "en" is better than nothing. But a platform-neutral protocol shouldn't hardcode English. The renderer can default to the host's locale? The HTML renderer has no host. Options:
- Host (session/starter) provides a default locale to the renderer (`render_document(..., options)`), default "en" if absent.
- Or emit `lang="en"` as the built-in default and document it. Since the existing title default is "Pathland", a default lang is acceptable for the reference renderer. But a French app that forgets metadata gets wrong lang; still better than missing for Lighthouse. I'd default to "en" in the HTML renderer and let apps override. Or the starter passes the app's default locale from config. Plan: renderer default "en", overridable by WINDOW_LOCALE; starters expose a config default.

Now, `PathlandSession` has `base` and mount; origin/canonical not addressed (deferred, host-level).

Also the **HTML `<title>`**: use WINDOW_TITLE; if absent keep "Pathland" (host configurable default later).

Now, **native window title mapping**: GTK `run(app_id, title, ...)` initial title stays; on META metadata, set the window title. Qt similarly. But the renderer's `run` currently takes the title once. Adding runtime updates requires the pump to hold the `gtk::ApplicationWindow`/Qt window handle and apply. This is feasible. If the scope is web-first, defer. Ask.

Now, **frame merge/rebase/proxy**:
- `FrameRebase`: if category META and command SET_WINDOW_METADATA and B's valueType == STRING, `c += base`.
- `FrameMerger`/`ProxySession`: drop window metadata from proxy origin frames (a proxied subtree must not retitle the host window). In `ProxySession` when remapping, filter the command. In `FrameMerger`, filter extras. Also live proxy deltas go through `ProxySession` → `frameSink`; filter there.
- Top-level app's metadata passes.

Now, **RESET**: don't clear window metadata (like theme). Document.

Now, **spec/CONFORMANCE**: vector for title/description/locale, plus a PROXY test.

Now, **tests**: as before.

Now, naming of the Java DSL modifier and types. Let me check the modifier naming conventions: `environmentBinding`, `borderedButtonStyle`. For a value type, `WindowMetadata` implementing `ViewModifier`, built via `Modifiers.windowMetadata(...)`. Fields: `title(String/Signal<String>)`, `description(...)`, `locale(...)`. Also maybe `WindowMetadata.title("...")` static? No, per convention use the facade. Actually style types have lowercase static factories on their own type (e.g. `BorderedButtonStyle.borderedButtonStyle(...)`), while modifiers are on `Modifiers`. Our type is a modifier, so `Modifiers.windowMetadata(...)`. Good.

Hmm: `Modifiers` is static-imported. `import static com.pathland.view.Modifiers.*;` gives `windowMetadata(...)`.

Now the Rust DSL surface naming: `pathland_view::window_metadata(...)`? Rust DSL uses newtypes `Padding(16.0)`, etc. A `WindowMetadata` value passed to a root? Since the Rust tree is nodes, the DSL could expose a `ViewExt::window_metadata(WindowMetadata)` that attaches metadata to the root `Node` (special fields) or emits via the engine. The cleanest: `Engine::window_metadata(WindowMetadata)` in `pathland-engine`, not the view DSL. Rust demo calls it. A DSL wrapper can be added later. For parity, not essential for the user's web case.

Now the plan should ask: scope (web vs also native). And naming (window vs app). And whether subtitle/canonical included.

Potential pushback: `WINDOW_DESCRIPTION` on web maps to meta description, which is web/SEO-specific. But the *concept* is general; the mapping is renderer-specific. That's exactly what the user wants. Good.

Now answer. Since plan mode, no edits. I should acknowledge the correction, then present the revised protocol-neutral design and plan. Ask 2-3 questions.

Let me make the plan not too long but complete. Use sections:

**Correction accepted**
- Rename concept: `META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` (0x08), field family.
- Table of fields and renderer mappings.
- Canonical/robots stay host/web concerns.

**Plan**
1. Spec/core/constants/conformance.
2. Rust engine + DSL (window metadata bindings; native host titles).
3. Java DSL/emitter (`WindowMetadata` modifier, signals, sink methods).
4. Renderers: HTML head, TS DOM, GTK/Qt window chrome.
5. SSR/session wiring and proxy filtering.
6. Demo usage (route title via computed signal).
7. Remaining a11y/SEO fixes (list).
8. Tests/verification.

**Questions** (use question tool):
Q1 Naming: `SET_WINDOW_METADATA` (recommended) vs `SET_APP_METADATA` vs `SET_SURFACE_METADATA`.
Q2 Fields: Title+Description+Locale (recommended) vs add Subtitle now vs only Title+Description.
Q3 Scope: Web path first (recommended) vs full parity incl. Rust engine + GTK/Qt titles now.
Maybe Q4 robots.txt/sitemap included? Could fold into scope or ask separately. Keep to 3-4.

Hmm, the question tool asks questions with options and returns answers; but the user might answer in text. Let's use it for structured choices. Ensure "Recommended" first.

Wait, the system reminder says plan mode active, read-only. The question tool is fine. But the user's last message is a correction; they may expect a revised plan, not a flurry of questions. I'll present the plan with a clear recommendation and ask only the critical scope question(s).

Let me refine the protocol names:
- Command: `SET_WINDOW_METADATA` value `0x08`. 
- Fields:
  - `TITLE` `0x0001`
  - `DESCRIPTION` `0x0002`
  - `LOCALE` `0x0003`
  - Maybe `SUBTITLE` `0x0004` (future).
- Encoding: A=fieldId, B=valueType (STRING=0x05), C=string offset. Empty string = clear.
- Direction: guest→host.
- Semantics: renderer-global presentation metadata for the host window/surface containing the stream; not part of the tree; survives `META::RESET`; re-emitted on full snapshot; ignored from proxied origins.

Renderer mappings table:
| Renderer | TITLE | DESCRIPTION | LOCALE |
| HTML/SSR | `<title>` | `<meta name=description>` | `<html lang>` |
| DOM client | `document.title` | meta description content | `document.documentElement.lang` |
| GTK4 | `GtkWindow`/headerbar title | headerbar subtitle / accessibility description | accessibility/lang (best-effort) |
| Qt | `QWindow::setTitle` | window subtitle (if available) / ignore | ignore |
| future TUI/native | terminal title / OS window title | status line / accessibility | locale |

Canonical and robots: host/web-owned; not protocol.

Now, is `LOCALE` really "window metadata"? Maybe better as a separate `META::SET_LOCALE`? But the field family is fine. Hmm, title/description/locale are all "presentation metadata of the surface". Okay.

Maybe name the family `SET_PRESENTATION`? "Window metadata" is clearer.

Now think about "description" on native: GTK headerbar subtitle; macOS no window subtitle until recent macOS (NSWindow.subtitle exists since 11). Fine.

Now the Rust engine API:
```rust
pub enum WindowField { Title, Description, Locale }
impl Engine {

Agreed — `SET_DOCUMENT_METADATA` was the wrong framing. The protocol concept should be **the host surface's presentation metadata** (window/app/shell), with the browser as one mapping.

## Revised protocol concept

**`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA` (`0x08`, guest → host)** — an extensible field family, like `META::ENVIRONMENT`:

| Field | ID | Encoding | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `WINDOW_TITLE` | `0x0001` | string offset (`B`) | Title of the window/app shell hosting this stream |
| `WINDOW_DESCRIPTION` | `0x0002` | string offset (`B`) | Human-readable description of the current content |
| `WINDOW_LOCALE` | `0x0003` | string offset (`B`) | BCP-47 content locale |
| *(future)* `WINDOW_SUBTITLE`, `WINDOW_ICON`, `WINDOW_MODIFIED` | | | |

Encoding: `A = fieldId (u16)`, `B = string offset` (same relative/arena convention as `SET_TEXT`/`ROUTE`), `C = 0`. Empty string clears the field. Renderer-global, not tree state; survives `META::RESET`; re-emitted on a full snapshot; ignored from proxied origins.

**Renderer mappings (renderer-defined, not protocol-defined):**

| Renderer | TITLE | DESCRIPTION | LOCALE |
|---|---|---|---|
| HTML/SSR | `<title>` | `<meta name="description">` | `<html lang>` |
| DOM client | `document.title` | meta description | `document.documentElement.lang` |
| GTK4 | `GtkWindow` / headerbar title | headerbar subtitle / a11y description | a11y/locale (best effort) |
| Qt | `QQuickWindow::setTitle` | window subtitle / ignore | ignore |
| future TUI/embedded | terminal/OS window title | status line / a11y | locale |

Web-only concerns stay **out** of the protocol: `canonical`, `robots`, sitemap. The web host derives those from the request URL/config, not from opcodes.

## Authoring surface (reactive)

Root-scoped `WindowMetadata` view modifier with signal-backed fields:

```java
root.modifiers(windowMetadata(w -> w
    .title(computed(() -> titleFor(router.path())))
    .description(computed(() -> descriptionFor(router.path())))
    .locale("en")));
```

- Mount emits the initial values in the SSR frame → correct `<title>`/description/lang on first paint.
- Each non-constant field gets an emitter effect; a signal change emits only that `META` opcode (unchanged → zero).
- A route change recomputes the title from the router signal → one opcode → the browser tab/native window title updates live.
- `renderFull()` re-emits the current metadata for resync.
- Rust parity: `Engine::bind_window_metadata(WindowMetadata { title: Option<Signal<String>>, … })`, with the same change detection in `set_signal`.

1. **Spec + core + conformance**

Another subtlety: `renderFull()` should re-emit window metadata (for resync). It calls `emitTheme()`; add `emitWindowMetadata()` (emit all fields regardless of dedupe? Dedupe against last emitted is fine, but a resync to a *fresh* client means the client has nothing; the server's `renderFull` is sent to a client that may have just reconnected with a cleared tree, but the head/title likely persists in the browser tab across reconnects. On a same-tab reload, SSR gives the head. On a resync after a gap, the title could have changed during the gap; re-emitting all fields ensures consistency. So `renderFull` should emit all non-empty fields unconditionally (like theme), not dedupe. Similarly, the mount frame emits all. The live delta path dedupes.

For the Rust engine, `emit()` is used for full snapshots? The engine's `emit` is diff; a full snapshot for resync is app-driven (maybe `Engine` has no full mode). Check `pathland-core` Guest `begin_frame`, and how the Rust demo responds to RESYNC. Not critical for the plan: emit metadata on change and on the first emit.

Now, **SSR head** in `HtmlRenderer`: It decodes the frame; metadata fields are strings. Add `WindowMeta` to `decode`. But `decode` also processes `META::RESET` etc. For metadata, later fields override earlier. Empty string clears. The head builder:
```rust
let lang = meta.locale.as_deref().unwrap_or("en");
format!("<!DOCTYPE html>\n<html lang=\"{}\"{scheme_attr}>...<title>{}</title>\n", ...)
```
Need to escape. `<meta name="description" content="...">` only if Some and non-empty. If description empty → omit.

Title: if empty/absent → "Pathland". Locale: if empty/absent → "en".

Now the session's `<html>` injection: `html.replace("<html>", ...)` will fail once lang is present. Change to `html.replacen("<html", "<html data-pathland-base=...")`? Java `String.replace("<html", ...)` would also replace in `<!DOCTYPE html>`? That's `<!DOCTYPE html>` lowercase "html" but not "<html". Only the actual tag. So `replace("<html", "<html data...")` is safe enough; but if the renderer emits `<html lang="en">`, result `<html data... lang="en">`. Fine. Use `replaceFirst(java.util.regex.Pattern.quote("<html"), ...)` or a small helper. Mention.

Also, the SSR session's fallback document (`renderer == null`) has `<html>`; unaffected.

Now, the **DOM client** `applyMeta` new signature with strings. Also, when hydrating, the client likely applies an initial full snapshot? The README says the client hydrates from SSR and only resyncs on reconnect; the initial metadata is in the head. If a `renderFull` arrives, applyMeta handles it. Fine.

Also `FrameMerger` rebases extras; but we drop metadata from proxies, so no need there; still add for correctness if the top-level frame is merged? `FrameMerger` merges base + extras; base is the host app's frame, extras are proxies. Need to track only when changed? `set_title` is cheap; compare to a stored value in the renderer (`window_title`) to avoid repeated changes. Add `GtkRenderer::window_title() -> Option<&str>` from RenderTree. In `pump_once` (no window), return? We can add a closure param or handle in the run loop after `pump_once`; the idle pump calls `pump_once`, then set title. Headerbar subtitle: `window` is `ApplicationWindow` with no built-in headerbar; nav pages have titles. For description, set the window's `accessible` description? - Add a `Guest::set_window_metadata`? The engine pushes directly; no need.

Now, **Java DSL**:
- `WindowMetadata` (config with Signals) + `WindowMetadataView` + `Modifiers.windowMetadata(...)`; `Environment` field.
- `WindowMetadata` should be a `ViewModifier`; the wrapper. Provide getters for the emitter.
- `OpcodeSink`: `setWindowMetadata(int field, String value)`; `FrameOpcodeSink` pushes with string table offset; `RingOpcodeSink` allocates into the arena and pushes.
- `Emitter`: bind + emit + dedupe + renderFull.

During render, environmentBinding renders inner → windowMetadata sets env. Fine. If the app applies windowMetadata inside `body()` of its root view, also fine. The emitter reads after render.

Now, **Environment** per session and structural re-render: the metadata wrapper sets `env` only when rendered. On structural swaps, the root isn't re-rendered, so the metadata stays as set at mount. That's intentional: root-scoped, reactive signals. Document that per-route metadata must be signal-driven (computed from the router), not a per-subtree constant.

The `pathland_native_*` C ABI could expose `pathland_native_bind_window_title(engine, signal)` for parity. Full parity might include it. Let's check `pathland-view-native/src` for signal APIs and whether adding metadata is warranted. The user's main path is Java/Web; but "full parity now" means Rust engine + GTK/Qt. The C ABI is for native hosts; the Rust engine API suffices for Rust demos. Adding C ABI is extra. We can mention "optional C ABI binding" or include it for completeness. | Field | ID | Encoding |
|---|---|---|

| `WINDOW_LOCALE` | `0x0003` | same |

Rules:
- Rendering-surface metadata, not tree state. Survives `META::RESET`; re-emitted on full snapshot.
- Empty string clears → renderer default.

 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
 > in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Java with the hand-written
 > **`com.pathland.view` DSL** (reusable library, Java 17+); both drive the engine
 > through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a zero-copy shared
 > ring on desktop.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
+- **Window metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, field family `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) carries the hosting surface's presentation metadata; renderers map it to their own chrome (browser `<title>`/meta description/`<html lang>`, GTK/Qt window title). It is root-scoped and signal-backed, so a route title is a computed over the router. Web-only artifacts (canonical/robots/sitemap) stay host-owned.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### no_std / wasm32 direction guard (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must remain `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and
 compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. This is the guarantee that the protocol
 core can still target a browser / embedded / remote projection later (goal #15,
 Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only
 consumer today, but the core must not become desktop-only. Verify with
 `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (i.e. `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view
 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
 
 ### Reactive signals (Angular-style)
 
 `pathland-core::signal` provides writable signals that live in the engine. A
 node binds its text (`Node::text_binding`), a property
 (`Node::property_bindings`) or a **string property** (`Node::string_bindings`,
 e.g. a media controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) to a `SignalId`; during emit the engine
 resolves the binding and records the dependency, and `Engine::set_signal`
 re-emits **only the bound nodes** (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`) — no full tree
 walk. Signal values
 are one of `F32`/`U32`/`Bool`/`Enum`/`Str` (packed to the wire's `u32` value or
 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI
 (`pathland_native_signal_create_*` / `signal_set_*` / `node_bind_text` /
 `node_bind_property`) and the Java `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`
 records the dependency; a subsequent `set` is a partial emit. (Computed/derived
 signals + effects are the planned next step.)
